attempts.summary: Built an IKEv2/IPsec site-to-site tunnel between node1 and node2 (OPNsense 26.1) over their shared transit network (172.16.100.0/30), carrying private traffic between node3's lan-a (10.50.10.0/24) and node4's lan-b (10.50.20.0/24). Configured via swanctl (strongSwan/vici) model in config.xml: new opt1 (transit, static) and opt2 (private LAN, static) interfaces on each firewall, a PSK-authenticated IKEv2 connection with a tunnel-mode child SA covering the two private CIDRs, and firewall rules permitting IKE/NAT-T/ESP on the transit interface plus a pass rule on a manually-registered 'ipsec' (enc0) pseudo-interface for decrypted traffic (required because OPNsense's core filter compiler only recognizes interfaces present in config.xml's <interfaces> section, not the plugin's dynamic-only ipsec interface list). node3/node4 got static private IPs and routes to the peer subnet via ens7, persisted through /etc/network/interfaces.d. Verified end-to-end: ping between 10.50.10.2 and 10.50.20.2 succeeds, and tcpdump on the transit link during a ping showed only ESP packets (no plaintext), confirming encryption in transit. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (preserving the other three throughout), each showing a changed boot identity (kern.boottime for the OPNsense nodes, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for the Ubuntu nodes) and full recovery: OPNsense nodes auto-restored their opt1/opt2 interfaces, pf ruleset, and IPsec SA (strongswan auto-started and re-established); Ubuntu nodes' static ens7 config and routes persisted via ifupdown, and end-to-end ping across the tunnel succeeded after each of the four restarts.
